## Starbie: 3D printed case in Fusion 360 (8

![Screenshot 2026-10-15 204154](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/eFI1qbxtPGZmzLCX4oomo3SgE8LA1rVP/01b8ea38c8d77a3caada2c6f6f57185b29aa224f7d73901134e4b6cc1a51eed2.png)

 hours)

This session I designed a case for my Starbie PCB in Fusion 360. It's a two-part star-shaped case (lid and base) that follows the outline of my board, with everything planned so it can actually be printed and assembled.

**What I did**
- Modelled the lid and base from scratch, matching the star outline of my PCB.
- Imported STEP models of the real parts (XIAO ESP32-C3, OLED, MPU6050, DHT11, switches) so I could check that everything fits and cut the openings in exactly the right places.
- Designed the closing method: [e.g. the lid fits over a lip on the base and is held with screws / snaps on].
- Designed how the PCB is held in: I made specially sized holes for **heat-set inserts** in the base, so the board can be fixed down with screws. Heat inserts give a much stronger thread than screwing straight into plastic.
- Added tolerances of [e.g. 0.2-0.3 mm] around the parts and the lid joint so it will fit after printing on my Bambu A1.
- Engraved the name "Starbie" into the lid as a custom detail.
- Made a render of the finished case and an assembly animation that shows the lid, PCB and base coming together.

**What worked and what didnt**
- My idea with overall looks worked quite nicely
-Had to watch a few youtube tutorials on few things

**What I learned**
- How to bring STEP models into a Fusion design and use them as references.
- Why tolerances matter for 3D printing, and how heat-set inserts are placed in a design.
- How to make a render and an exploded assembly animation.

**Next:** print the case on my A1 to test the fit once my parts arrive.

## Starbie: organising my GitHub repos (40 minutes)

This session I tidied up my project files on GitHub so that everything is easy to find.

**What I did**
- Created a separate repo, CAD-enclosure, for my case design, with the Fusion 360 file, the STL and 3MF print files, and the render and screenshots of my design process.
- Wrote a README for the CAD repo that lists the design features and files.
- Checked that the file paths and images in the READMEs work, and that the Status list is accurate.

**What I learned**
- How to organise a project across more than one repo, and link them together.
- Why a clear README matters: it's how someone else finds and understands the files.
